newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Ed nuke seen down at least 6 weeks.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Ed nuke seen down at least 6 weeks.

text.p: Detroit Edison's Fermi 2 nuclear power plant will be shut at least six more weeks while the company completes maintenance on a generator rotor, a spokeswoman said Wednesday.
The six weeks are needed for machining and high-speed balancing of the plant generator's rotor at an offsite facility, the spokeswoman said.
The plant, which has a rated capacity of 1,116 megawatts (MW), had been operating at 1,075 MW previous to a shutdown Sept 27 for scheduled maintenance.
Since the shutdown, a full resumption of production from the plant has been delayed by a series of technical problems.

The failure of an electrical component in a switchyard outside the plant resulted in an electrical current entering the plant's generator on Jan 17, which caused excessive heating of the rotor, the spokeswoman said.

Fermi 2 is located in Newport, Mich., and makes up about 15 percent of Detroit Edison's power generation capacity. The company supplies about two million southeast Michigan customers with electricity.
Detroit Edison is a subsidiary of DTE Energy Co.
